subject: Physics
paperTitle: Paper 3 Section B Option B — Medical physics
sourceVerification: All 12 official part marks and original page positions checked against AQA June 2022 QP and final MS. AQA specification codes verified against official 3.10 page. Q04 is cross-topic imaging comparison; primary 3.10.6.6 used with 3.10.4.1, 3.10.4.3, 3.10.5.4.
markingGuidanceOriginalSummary: The eye-lens calculation has distinguishable method, substitution and result credit; a wrong sign restricts full marks.
The radiographic energy estimate allows different calculation orders and consequential arithmetic marking.
Drawn loudness-response curves need a valid axis scale and visible minimum; plain text is not sufficient evidence.
The six-mark imaging decision is level-based, not a keyword checklist.
Conflicting statements may cancel otherwise correct points; accept valid alternative explanations within the official boundaries.
copyrightNotice: This is an original editorial source map, not an interactive paper. No AQA question wording, diagram, answer key or detailed marking text is reproduced.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Vision defect corrected by converging lens
parts.markingRisk: Correct defect classification rather than unrelated optical labels.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Corrective lens magnification from power and distance
parts.markingRisk: Independent method, substitution and final-value marks; sign mistakes cap available credit.
Identification mark is linked to the complete set; function marks can stand independently.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Detector choice for a static radiographic image
parts.markingRisk: Selection, reasons and contextual trade-offs need separate credit; no-selection response has a lower maximum.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Attenuation-based estimate of absorbed X-ray energy
parts.markingRisk: Equivalent calculation orders accepted; transmitted, absorbed, area, power and energy stages are separable.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Limitations of a simplified X-ray absorption estimate
parts.markingRisk: Specific geometric or prior tissue-absorption assumptions are needed, not generic uncertainty.
Lowest-frequency response point and scale must be supported by the drawn curve; a prose description cannot earn graph marks.
Compare varying frequencies to a reference, adjusting amplitude for equal perceived loudness.
Check logarithm base, reference intensity and units; algebraic alternatives accepted.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Selecting medical imaging for a particular clinical context
parts.markingRisk: Assess overall comparison of image quality, safety and practical factors; top levels require a justified choice.
Do not conflate proton spin alignment with atom alignment.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Radio-frequency pulses in magnetic resonance imaging
parts.markingRisk: Credit two valid distinct pulse/excitation/relaxation points, not duplicated synonyms.
